extracted.intended_audience: general readers / comedy fans and casual viewers (people curious what a Roast Battle is)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and informal rules for the live comedy format 'Roast Battle' — head-to-head insult-based rounds run as a bracketed tournament for comedians, intended for performers and viewers to understand format, preparation, and norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-comedian mic-to-mic verbal combat
rubrics_metrics.description: Two comedians going mic to mic in verbal combat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head-to-head exchange of insults on stage; the format is an in-person, direct confrontation using jokes rather than physical aggression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tournament / bracketed structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comedy Central Show is like a March Madness style bracketed tournament or a home run derby of roasting. Sixteen comedians are making their way to the final championship battle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitors advance through rounds/semifinals to a final; the event is structured as a multi-round elimination contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: research your opponent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedians prepare targeted material by researching their opponent to craft personalized roast jokes and angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set length / material: do your 4 or 5 best jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: They research each other, do their 4 or 5 best jokes, and sometimes it goes to sudden death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform concise, high-quality material (typically 4–5 jokes) rather than long routines; prioritize strongest bits for the battle format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules are you have to be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should be original to the performer (no recycled or stolen bits); originality is an explicit rule of the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: No topic is off-limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is off limits as far as topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roasts permit addressing sensitive or taboo subjects; performers are expected to push boundaries within this ethos (though broader social/production norms may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiebreaker: sudden death
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes it goes to sudden death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If judges cannot decide a clear winner after the scheduled material, additional rounds or sudden-death exchanges determine the victor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every battle ends with a hug
rubrics_metrics.description: Every battle ends with a hug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite harsh insults delivered during the battle, a ritualized reconciliation (hug) signals camaraderie and sportsmanship after the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee / host enforces non-physical resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Brian Moses ... said 'don't fight you guys, go home, write some jokes, come back tomorrow and have a roast battle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The referee/host role is to channel conflict into comedic performance rather than physical fights; they organize and enforce the format and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging: decide who’s funnier (subjective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jimmy Kimmel ... called it unbelievably funny. Ross told him his job was basically to get wasted and decide who’s funnier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners are chosen by judges (often celebrities); judging is ultimately subjective and based on perceived funniness rather than a strict point system.
